title: Can Japan’s Defense Industry Meet its Ambitious Goals?
author: Hana Vogeley
text:
MHI launched Tatsuta, the eleventh Mogami-class frigate on order for the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force, in a ceremony held at its facilities in Nagasaki, Japan, July 2, 2025.
Credit: Takahashi Kosuke
On August 4, the Japanese Ministry of Defense published its annual 2026 Defense White Paper, which outlines Japan’s defense policies and activities. While the report extensively covers the increasingly severe security environment surrounding Japan, notable highlights include an emphasis on one of Japan’s core concepts, “new ways of defense,” and its defense production.  Notably, the White Paper follows Japanese Defense Minister Koizumi Shinjiro’s comment at the Farnborough International Airshow: “Defense production is deterrence itself. No matter how advanced a defense system may be, it means little if it cannot be produced.” His statement suggests a fundamental shift in how Japan views deterrence: rather than mere possession of defense materiel, Japan increasingly recognizes the importance of the defense industrial base as a source of strategic capability.   [...]
